prompt:
A diagonal view across the open-plan floor towards the corner where the glazed facade turns, cutting obliquely across the desk bands.

General material and lighting reference (use unless contradicted below):
Material and lighting style: Light neutral floor with a seamless finish. Walls are a textured light hue. Ceiling combines bare structural elements with suspended wooden islands, adding a dynamic contrast. Desks feature light wood with crisp edges. Chairs are ergonomically designed with black frames and dark upholstery. Partitioning includes curved frosted glass, creating privacy without heaviness. Metal finishes are minimal, accentuating a clean and modern feel. The overall tone is warm with sufficient soft daylight, complemented by recessed luminaires providing even, natural lighting.

Interior architectural photography, 24 mm tilt-shift lens, two-point perspective with perfectly straight vertical lines, soft overcast daylight from the floor-to-ceiling glazing, realistic material response, natural dynamic range, crisp detail, no text, no signage, no CG or 3D-render look.

FIXED DESIGN DECISIONS — these override anything above, follow every line exactly:
· acoustic ceiling rafts floating over the desk bands, with the painted soffit and services exposed over the circulation
· white horizontal venetian blinds with the slats half open
· large square luminous grid panels suspended on slim rods below the soffit, glowing evenly, with slim black track spotlights alongside
· plain light grey vinyl flooring
· light oak and white furniture with simple square-edge profiles
· no desk screens at all, plain open bench desks
· a warm timber and neutral palette
· no people in the frame

MEASURED FROM THE BUILDING DRAWINGS — these are facts, not preferences. Never change them, whatever the reference photograph or the style description shows:
· The facade is a FULL-HEIGHT GLASS CURTAIN WALL. The glass starts at the finished floor and runs up to 4230 mm, just under the slab soffit. There is NO window sill, NO spandrel panel, NO solid wall below the glass, and NO separate punched window openings — it is one continuous glazed wall divided only by slim vertical mullions.
· The mullions are spaced 4050 mm apart. Do not draw a denser window grid.
· Ceiling height above the finished floor: 3000 mm. Do not lower it.
· Main aisle 1800 mm, secondary aisles 1400 mm. Do not narrow them.
· This frame contains at least 12 clearly readable workstations (one desk position plus one task chair each), with more receding into the distance, at least 4 vertical curtain-wall mullions. Show no fewer than that, and do not close the room off with a wall that is not in the reference, shorten it, or thin out the desk rows.
· Down the left of this frame is the curtain wall described above — glazing, not wall.
· Down the right of this frame, taking about 4% of the frame, is a SERVICES RISER: a flush metal access door with no visible handle, painted to match the wall. The massing model shows it as blank wall only because the door is not modelled — the door is really there, so put it in. Never leave that wall blank.

The reference image is an UNTEXTURED WHITE MASSING MODEL — every surface is placeholder grey, there is no material, colour or lighting information in it whatsoever. Take ONLY the geometry, camera and object positions from it. Invent all materials, colours, textures and lighting yourself, strictly following the fixed design decisions below.

The reference image is a SIMPLIFIED MASSING MODEL, not a finished render. Every plain block in it is a placeholder standing for a real object at that exact position, size and orientation. Replace each placeholder with properly detailed real-world furniture and fittings: ergonomic mesh-back task chairs with contoured seats, adjustable armrests, gas lift and five-star castor bases; bench desk systems with slim square legs, under-desk cable trays and cable grommets; slim-bezel monitors on articulated arms, keyboards and mice; a few believable personal items. Keep unchanged: the camera and framing, the room shape, the number of desks and chairs, the aisle widths, the ceiling height, and the window mullion spacing.
